column74: The Health Ministry has issued revised guidelines for international arrivals, with effect from February 14, doing away with the mandatory seven-day home quarantine and the need for them to undertake an RT-PCR test on the eighth day.  Apart from uploading a negative RT-PCR report for unvaccinated, taken 72 hours before the journey, there is an option to upload certificates of the completion of the full primary Covid vaccination schedule provided from countries on a reciprocal basis. On arrivals, ALL passengers will undergo thermal screening, and any symptomatic passenger will be isolated as per standard norms. Furthermore, about 2% of overall passengers in any given flight would undergo random testing at the airports on arrival. International travellers arriving through seaports/land ports will also have to undergo the same protocol as above, except that facility for online registration is not available for such passengers currently.    Archived Link: https://web.archive.org/web/20220313200632/https://www.mohfw.gov.in/pdf/GuidelinesforInternationalarrivalsupdatedon10thFebruary2022.pdf

column88: https://web.archive.org/web/20220323132631/https://www.mha.gov.in/sites/default/files/MHAOrderCOVIDContainment_25022022.pdf  MHA order dated 25 Feb 2022  "Ensure sustained critical level of testing as per the testing guidelines"    https://archive.ph/jGI1E  ICMR Purposive testing strategy dated 10 Jan 2022  ""People who need not be tested: Contacts of confirmed cases of Covid unless identified as high risk based on age or comorbidities and individuals undertaking inter-state domestic travel," read the ICMR Advisory on Purposive Testing Strategy for COVID-19 issued on Monday.  The new strategy has invoked mixed reactions. Public health expert Dr Chandrakant Lahariya told India Today, "At this stage of the pandemic, especially when Omicron has a high rate of transmission and many are asymptomatic, the benefit of testing of asymptomatic (or even mild symptomatic) is far reduced.  "It does not serve the purpose of better case management at individual level or a major dent in reducing transmission. Therefore, the revised policy by ICMR is epidemiologically sound. It will achieve public health purposes in an efficient way," Dr Lahariya said.Dr Chandrakant Lahariya also said that this new advisory, when combined with the new discharge policy, is a paradigm shift in public health response to the Covid-19 pandemic."  https://archive.ph/dUhbG

column88: ICMR advisory on purposive testing as of 10 Jan 2022 still stands, allows anyone to procure a RTPCR test   https://archive.vn/F8aFB  "Who may be tested:  A. In community settings:  1. Symptomatic (cough, fever, sore throat, loss of taste and/or smell, breathlessness and/or  other respiratory symptoms) individuals.  2. At-risk contacts of laboratory confirmed cases.  [At-risk contacts are elderly (>60yr) and individuals with co-morbidity such as diabetes,  hypertension, chronic lung or kidney disease, malignancy, obesity etc].  3. Individuals undertaking international travel (as per country-specific requirements).  4. International travelers arriving at Indian airports/seaports/ports of entries as per laid down  guidelines.  B. In Hospital Settings:  5. Testing may be undertaken as per discretion of the treating doctor with the following  considerations:  ? No emergency procedure (including surgeries and deliveries) should be delayed for lack  of a test.  ? Patients should not be referred to other facilities for lack of a testing facility. All  arrangements should be made to collect and transfer samples to testing facilities,  mapped to the health facility.  ? Asymptomatic patients undergoing surgical / non-surgical invasive procedures including  pregnant women in/near labour who are hospitalized for delivery should not be tested  unless warranted or symptoms develop."

column74: The Health Ministry has issued revised guidelines for international arrivals, with effect from February 14, doing away with the mandatory seven-day home quarantine and the need for them to undertake an RT-PCR test on the eighth day. Apart from uploading a negative RT-PCR report for unvaccinated, taken 72 hours before the journey, there is an option to upload certificates of the completion of the full primary Covid vaccination schedule provided from countries on a reciprocal basis. On arrivals, ALL passengers will undergo thermal screening, and any symptomatic passenger will be isolated as per standard norms. Furthermore, about 2% of overall passengers in any given flight would undergo random testing at the airports on arrival. International travellers arriving through seaports/land ports will also have to undergo the same protocol as above, except that facility for online registration is not available for such passengers currently. column15: https://archive.ph/xG76k  GUWAHATI: Assam will reopen completely from February 15 as the Covid cases have dipped significantly. He, however, said the students appearing for the exams must be fully vaccinated. The moratoriums will be applicable to borrowers with a maximum total exposure of 250 million rupees ($3.39 million), Das said." - https://archive.ph/ZMwPq#selection-295.0-298.0 May 5 2021  https://web.archive.org/web/20230509142449/https://www.reuters.com/world/india/india-cenbank-allows-fresh-moratorium-some-small-borrowers-amid-covid-19-crisis-2021-05-05/  Some form of debt relief seems to be continuing, as seen from the national government recently approving further allocations to reimburse lenders to support the loan moratorium scheme, which would presumably in turn support the ability to offer debt relief for borrowers, including households. 1. 19 Jan 2022: "Goverment to pay Rs 974 crore more to lenders towards loan moratorium scheme" https://web.archive.org/web/20220120075321/https://www.newindianexpress.com/nation/2022/jan/19/govermentto-pay-rs-974-cr-more-to-lenders-towards-loan-moratorium-scheme-2408753.html 2. 20 Jan 2022: “By granting ex-gratia payment of difference between compound interest and simple interest during the six month moratorium period to distressed/vulnerable category of borrowers, irrespective of whether the borrower had availed of moratorium or not, the scheme would equitably help small borrowers bear the stress on account of the pandemic and get back on their feet, said an official release.” https://web.archive.org/web/20220207205127/https://zeenews.india.com/personal-finance/big-relief-for-borrowers-on-loan-moratorium-cabinet-sanctions-rs-973-crore-2429276.html 3. “The COVID-related restructuring scheme was first announced by Reserve Bank of India in August 2020 for both retail and corporate borrowers, and was then extended in May last year after a resurgence in COVID cases. column15: All offices, shops, and business establishments, all religious places, and shopping malls would now be opened in a normal way since february 7 as the Bihar government decided to lift many COVID-19 restrictions citing improvement in pandemic situation. However, visitors to these places will have to wear masks, maintain social distance and follow Covid-19 related norms.  In the wake of improvement in the situation of the covid-19 infection, all schools up to class-8 can be opened with 50% attendance. The schools of class- 9 and above, the colleges and coaching institutes can be opened with 100 per cent attendance. All government offices will be opened on all working days in a normal way. Entry of only vaccinated visitors will be allowed in the offices  Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20220315105730/https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/patna/bihar-covid-related-restrictions-lifted-offices-shops-religious-places-to-open-from-february-7/articleshow/89389611.cms

The new strategy has invoked mixed reactions. Public health expert Dr Chandrakant Lahariya told India Today, "At this stage of the pandemic, especially when Omicron has a high rate of transmission and many are asymptomatic, the benefit of testing of asymptomatic (or even mild symptomatic) is far reduced.  "It does not serve the purpose of better case management at individual level or a major dent in reducing transmission. Therefore, the revised policy by ICMR is epidemiologically sound. It will achieve public health purposes in an efficient way," Dr Lahariya said.Dr Chandrakant Lahariya also said that this new advisory, when combined with the new discharge policy, is a paradigm shift in public health response to the Covid-19 pandemic."  https://archive.ph/dUhbG

The new strategy has invoked mixed reactions. Public health expert Dr Chandrakant Lahariya told India Today, "At this stage of the pandemic, especially when Omicron has a high rate of transmission and many are asymptomatic, the benefit of testing of asymptomatic (or even mild symptomatic) is far reduced.  "It does not serve the purpose of better case management at individual level or a major dent in reducing transmission. Therefore, the revised policy by ICMR is epidemiologically sound. It will achieve public health purposes in an efficient way," Dr Lahariya said.Dr Chandrakant Lahariya also said that this new advisory, when combined with the new discharge policy, is a paradigm shift in public health response to the Covid-19 pandemic."  https://archive.ph/dUhbG

column88: ICMR advisory on purposive testing as of 10 Jan 2022 still stands, allows anyone to procure a RTPCR test   https://archive.vn/F8aFB  "Who may be tested:  A. In community settings:  1. Symptomatic (cough, fever, sore throat, loss of taste and/or smell, breathlessness and/or  other respiratory symptoms) individuals.  2. At-risk contacts of laboratory confirmed cases.  [At-risk contacts are elderly (>60yr) and individuals with co-morbidity such as diabetes,  hypertension, chronic lung or kidney disease, malignancy, obesity etc].  3. Individuals undertaking international travel (as per country-specific requirements).  4. International travelers arriving at Indian airports/seaports/ports of entries as per laid down  guidelines.  B. In Hospital Settings:  5. Testing may be undertaken as per discretion of the treating doctor with the following  considerations:  ? No emergency procedure (including surgeries and deliveries) should be delayed for lack  of a test.  ? Patients should not be referred to other facilities for lack of a testing facility. All  arrangements should be made to collect and transfer samples to testing facilities,  mapped to the health facility.  ? Asymptomatic patients undergoing surgical / non-surgical invasive procedures including  pregnant women in/near labour who are hospitalized for delivery should not be tested  unless warranted or symptoms develop."
column90: https://archive.ph/jGI1E  ICMR Purposive testing strategy dated 10 Jan 2022  ""People who need not be tested: Contacts of confirmed cases of Covid unless identified as high risk based on age or comorbidities and individuals undertaking inter-state domestic travel," read the ICMR Advisory on Purposive Testing Strategy for COVID-19 issued on Monday.  The new strategy has invoked mixed reactions. Public health expert Dr Chandrakant Lahariya told India Today, "At this stage of the pandemic, especially when Omicron has a high rate of transmission and many are asymptomatic, the benefit of testing of asymptomatic (or even mild symptomatic) is far reduced.  "It does not serve the purpose of better case management at individual level or a major dent in reducing transmission. Therefore, the revised policy by ICMR is epidemiologically sound. It will achieve public health purposes in an efficient way," Dr Lahariya said.Dr Chandrakant Lahariya also said that this new advisory, when combined with the new discharge policy, is a paradigm shift in public health response to the Covid-19 pandemic."  https://archive.ph/dUhbG

column119: The Hindu) Chhattisgarh government suspends COVID-19 vaccination for 18-44 age group (6th May 2022)    -The Chhattisgarh government has suspended the third phase of COVID-19 vaccination drive for people aged 18 to 44, after the high court’s order to modify the plan that prioritised inoculation of the economically weaker sections of society, an official said on Thursday.  -The State government in an order on April 30 said vaccines will be first given to the Antyodaya group (poorest among poor), followed by those in the below poverty line (BPL) category and then to people in the above poverty line (APL) group, in the third phase of the drive that began on May 1.  -The vaccination for people aged above 45 years will continue in the State, the official added.    https://web.archive.org/web/20230223160830/https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/other-states/chhattisgarh-government-suspends-covid-19-vaccination-for-18-44-age-group/article34498493.ece

column90: https://archive.ph/jGI1E  ICMR Purposive testing strategy dated 10 Jan 2022  ""People who need not be tested: Contacts of confirmed cases of Covid unless identified as high risk based on age or comorbidities and individuals undertaking inter-state domestic travel," read the ICMR Advisory on Purposive Testing Strategy for COVID-19 issued on Monday.  The new strategy has invoked mixed reactions. Public health expert Dr Chandrakant Lahariya told India Today, "At this stage of the pandemic, especially when Omicron has a high rate of transmission and many are asymptomatic, the benefit of testing of asymptomatic (or even mild symptomatic) is far reduced.  "It does not serve the purpose of better case management at individual level or a major dent in reducing transmission. Therefore, the revised policy by ICMR is epidemiologically sound. It will achieve public health purposes in an efficient way," Dr Lahariya said.Dr Chandrakant Lahariya also said that this new advisory, when combined with the new discharge policy, is a paradigm shift in public health response to the Covid-19 pandemic."  https://archive.ph/dUhbG

column90: https://archive.ph/jGI1E  ICMR Purposive testing strategy dated 10 Jan 2022  ""People who need not be tested: Contacts of confirmed cases of Covid unless identified as high risk based on age or comorbidities and individuals undertaking inter-state domestic travel," read the ICMR Advisory on Purposive Testing Strategy for COVID-19 issued on Monday.  The new strategy has invoked mixed reactions. Public health expert Dr Chandrakant Lahariya told India Today, "At this stage of the pandemic, especially when Omicron has a high rate of transmission and many are asymptomatic, the benefit of testing of asymptomatic (or even mild symptomatic) is far reduced.  "It does not serve the purpose of better case management at individual level or a major dent in reducing transmission. Therefore, the revised policy by ICMR is epidemiologically sound. It will achieve public health purposes in an efficient way," Dr Lahariya said.Dr Chandrakant Lahariya also said that this new advisory, when combined with the new discharge policy, is a paradigm shift in public health response to the Covid-19 pandemic."  https://archive.ph/dUhbG

column74: The Health Ministry has issued revised guidelines for international arrivals, with effect from February 14, doing away with the mandatory seven-day home quarantine and the need for them to undertake an RT-PCR test on the eighth day. The new strategy has invoked mixed reactions. Public health expert Dr Chandrakant Lahariya told India Today, "At this stage of the pandemic, especially when Omicron has a high rate of transmission and many are asymptomatic, the benefit of testing of asymptomatic (or even mild symptomatic) is far reduced.  "It does not serve the purpose of better case management at individual level or a major dent in reducing transmission. Therefore, the revised policy by ICMR is epidemiologically sound. It will achieve public health purposes in an efficient way," Dr Lahariya said.Dr Chandrakant Lahariya also said that this new advisory, when combined with the new discharge policy, is a paradigm shift in public health response to the Covid-19 pandemic."  https://archive.ph/dUhbG

column90: https://archive.ph/jGI1E  ICMR Purposive testing strategy dated 10 Jan 2022  ""People who need not be tested: Contacts of confirmed cases of Covid unless identified as high risk based on age or comorbidities and individuals undertaking inter-state domestic travel," read the ICMR Advisory on Purposive Testing Strategy for COVID-19 issued on Monday.  The new strategy has invoked mixed reactions. Public health expert Dr Chandrakant Lahariya told India Today, "At this stage of the pandemic, especially when Omicron has a high rate of transmission and many are asymptomatic, the benefit of testing of asymptomatic (or even mild symptomatic) is far reduced.  "It does not serve the purpose of better case management at individual level or a major dent in reducing transmission. Therefore, the revised policy by ICMR is epidemiologically sound. It will achieve public health purposes in an efficient way," Dr Lahariya said.Dr Chandrakant Lahariya also said that this new advisory, when combined with the new discharge policy, is a paradigm shift in public health response to the Covid-19 pandemic."  https://archive.ph/dUhbG

column74: The Health Ministry has issued revised guidelines for international arrivals, with effect from February 14, doing away with the mandatory seven-day home quarantine and the need for them to undertake an RT-PCR test on the eighth day. Apart from uploading a negative RT-PCR report for unvaccinated, taken 72 hours before the journey, there is an option to upload certificates of the completion of the full primary Covid vaccination schedule provided from countries on a reciprocal basis. On arrivals, ALL passengers will undergo thermal screening, and any symptomatic passenger will be isolated as per standard norms. Furthermore, about 2% of overall passengers in any given flight would undergo random testing at the airports on arrival. International travellers arriving through seaports/land ports will also have to undergo the same protocol as above, except that facility for online registration is not available for such passengers currently. column88: ICMR advisory on purposive testing as of 10 Jan 2022 still stands, allows anyone to procure a RTPCR test   https://archive.vn/F8aFB  "Who may be tested:  A. In community settings:  1. Symptomatic (cough, fever, sore throat, loss of taste and/or smell, breathlessness and/or  other respiratory symptoms) individuals.  2. At-risk contacts of laboratory confirmed cases.  [At-risk contacts are elderly (>60yr) and individuals with co-morbidity such as diabetes,  hypertension, chronic lung or kidney disease, malignancy, obesity etc].  3. Individuals undertaking international travel (as per country-specific requirements).  4. International travelers arriving at Indian airports/seaports/ports of entries as per laid down  guidelines.  B. In Hospital Settings:  5. Testing may be undertaken as per discretion of the treating doctor with the following  considerations:  ? No emergency procedure (including surgeries and deliveries) should be delayed for lack  of a test.  ? Patients should not be referred to other facilities for lack of a testing facility. All  arrangements should be made to collect and transfer samples to testing facilities,  mapped to the health facility.  ? Asymptomatic patients undergoing surgical / non-surgical invasive procedures including  pregnant women in/near labour who are hospitalized for delivery should not be tested  unless warranted or symptoms develop."
column90: https://archive.ph/jGI1E  ICMR Purposive testing strategy dated 10 Jan 2022  ""People who need not be tested: Contacts of confirmed cases of Covid unless identified as high risk based on age or comorbidities and individuals undertaking inter-state domestic travel," read the ICMR Advisory on Purposive Testing Strategy for COVID-19 issued on Monday.  The new strategy has invoked mixed reactions. Public health expert Dr Chandrakant Lahariya told India Today, "At this stage of the pandemic, especially when Omicron has a high rate of transmission and many are asymptomatic, the benefit of testing of asymptomatic (or even mild symptomatic) is far reduced.  "It does not serve the purpose of better case management at individual level or a major dent in reducing transmission. Therefore, the revised policy by ICMR is epidemiologically sound. It will achieve public health purposes in an efficient way," Dr Lahariya said.Dr Chandrakant Lahariya also said that this new advisory, when combined with the new discharge policy, is a paradigm shift in public health response to the Covid-19 pandemic."  https://archive.ph/dUhbG

column90: https://web.archive.org/web/20220323132631/https://www.mha.gov.in/sites/default/files/MHAOrderCOVIDContainment_25022022.pdf    https://archive.ph/jGI1E  ICMR Purposive testing strategy dated 10 Jan 2022  ""People who need not be tested: Contacts of confirmed cases of Covid unless identified as high risk based on age or comorbidities and individuals undertaking inter-state domestic travel," read the ICMR Advisory on Purposive Testing Strategy for COVID-19 issued on Monday.  The new strategy has invoked mixed reactions. Public health expert Dr Chandrakant Lahariya told India Today, "At this stage of the pandemic, especially when Omicron has a high rate of transmission and many are asymptomatic, the benefit of testing of asymptomatic (or even mild symptomatic) is far reduced.  "It does not serve the purpose of better case management at individual level or a major dent in reducing transmission. Therefore, the revised policy by ICMR is epidemiologically sound. It will achieve public health purposes in an efficient way," Dr Lahariya said.Dr Chandrakant Lahariya also said that this new advisory, when combined with the new discharge policy, is a paradigm shift in public health response to the Covid-19 pandemic."  https://archive.ph/dUhbG

column74: The Health Ministry has issued revised guidelines for international arrivals, with effect from February 14, doing away with the mandatory seven-day home quarantine and the need for them to undertake an RT-PCR test on the eighth day.  Apart from uploading a negative RT-PCR report for unvaccinated, taken 72 hours before the journey, there is an option to upload certificates of the completion of the full primary Covid vaccination schedule provided from countries on a reciprocal basis. On arrivals, ALL passengers will undergo thermal screening, and any symptomatic passenger will be isolated as per standard norms. Furthermore, about 2% of overall passengers in any given flight would undergo random testing at the airports on arrival. International travellers arriving through seaports/land ports will also have to undergo the same protocol as above, except that facility for online registration is not available for such passengers currently. The new strategy has invoked mixed reactions. Public health expert Dr Chandrakant Lahariya told India Today, "At this stage of the pandemic, especially when Omicron has a high rate of transmission and many are asymptomatic, the benefit of testing of asymptomatic (or even mild symptomatic) is far reduced.  "It does not serve the purpose of better case management at individual level or a major dent in reducing transmission. Therefore, the revised policy by ICMR is epidemiologically sound. It will achieve public health purposes in an efficient way," Dr Lahariya said.Dr Chandrakant Lahariya also said that this new advisory, when combined with the new discharge policy, is a paradigm shift in public health response to the Covid-19 pandemic."  https://archive.ph/dUhbG

Travellers from specified Countries at risk [as mentioned in para (iii) above] will follow the protocol as detailed below:  ? Submission of sample for post-arrival COVID-19 test* at the point of arrival (self-paid). Such travellers will be required to wait for their test results at the arrival airport before leaving or taking a connecting flight.  ? If tested negative they will follow, home quarantine for 7 days. Re-test on the 8th day of arrival in India* and if negative, further self-monitor of their health for next 7 days.  ? However, if such travellers are tested positive, their samples should be sent for genomic testing at INSACOG laboratory network.  ? They shall be managed at separate isolation facility and treated as per laid down standard protocol including contact tracing mentioned in para (xiv).  ? column90: https://archive.ph/jGI1E  ICMR Purposive testing strategy dated 10 Jan 2022  ""People who need not be tested: Contacts of confirmed cases of Covid unless identified as high risk based on age or comorbidities and individuals undertaking inter-state domestic travel," read the ICMR Advisory on Purposive Testing Strategy for COVID-19 issued on Monday.  The new strategy has invoked mixed reactions. Public health expert Dr Chandrakant Lahariya told India Today, "At this stage of the pandemic, especially when Omicron has a high rate of transmission and many are asymptomatic, the benefit of testing of asymptomatic (or even mild symptomatic) is far reduced.  "It does not serve the purpose of better case management at individual level or a major dent in reducing transmission. Therefore, the revised policy by ICMR is epidemiologically sound. It will achieve public health purposes in an efficient way," Dr Lahariya said.Dr Chandrakant Lahariya also said that this new advisory, when combined with the new discharge policy, is a paradigm shift in public health response to the Covid-19 pandemic."  https://archive.ph/dUhbG

column88: https://web.archive.org/web/20220323132631/https://www.mha.gov.in/sites/default/files/MHAOrderCOVIDContainment_25022022.pdf  MHA order dated 25 Feb 2022  "Ensure sustained critical level of testing as per the testing guidelines"    https://archive.ph/jGI1E  ICMR Purposive testing strategy dated 10 Jan 2022  ""People who need not be tested: Contacts of confirmed cases of Covid unless identified as high risk based on age or comorbidities and individuals undertaking inter-state domestic travel," read the ICMR Advisory on Purposive Testing Strategy for COVID-19 issued on Monday.  The new strategy has invoked mixed reactions. Public health expert Dr Chandrakant Lahariya told India Today, "At this stage of the pandemic, especially when Omicron has a high rate of transmission and many are asymptomatic, the benefit of testing of asymptomatic (or even mild symptomatic) is far reduced.  "It does not serve the purpose of better case management at individual level or a major dent in reducing transmission. Therefore, the revised policy by ICMR is epidemiologically sound. It will achieve public health purposes in an efficient way," Dr Lahariya said.Dr Chandrakant Lahariya also said that this new advisory, when combined with the new discharge policy, is a paradigm shift in public health response to the Covid-19 pandemic."  https://archive.ph/dUhbG

ICMR advisory on purposive testing as of 10 Jan 2022 still stands, allows anyone to procure a RTPCR test   https://archive.vn/F8aFB  "Who may be tested:  A. In community settings:  1. Symptomatic (cough, fever, sore throat, loss of taste and/or smell, breathlessness and/or  other respiratory symptoms) individuals.  2. At-risk contacts of laboratory confirmed cases.  [At-risk contacts are elderly (>60yr) and individuals with co-morbidity such as diabetes,  hypertension, chronic lung or kidney disease, malignancy, obesity etc].  3. Individuals undertaking international travel (as per country-specific requirements).  4. International travelers arriving at Indian airports/seaports/ports of entries as per laid down  guidelines.  B. In Hospital Settings:  5. Testing may be undertaken as per discretion of the treating doctor with the following  considerations:  ? No emergency procedure (including surgeries and deliveries) should be delayed for lack  of a test.  ? Patients should not be referred to other facilities for lack of a testing facility. All  arrangements should be made to collect and transfer samples to testing facilities,  mapped to the health facility.  ? Asymptomatic patients undergoing surgical / non-surgical invasive procedures including  pregnant women in/near labour who are hospitalized for delivery should not be tested  unless warranted or symptoms develop."

column90: https://archive.ph/jGI1E  ICMR Purposive testing strategy dated 10 Jan 2022  ""People who need not be tested: Contacts of confirmed cases of Covid unless identified as high risk based on age or comorbidities and individuals undertaking inter-state domestic travel," read the ICMR Advisory on Purposive Testing Strategy for COVID-19 issued on Monday.  The new strategy has invoked mixed reactions. Public health expert Dr Chandrakant Lahariya told India Today, "At this stage of the pandemic, especially when Omicron has a high rate of transmission and many are asymptomatic, the benefit of testing of asymptomatic (or even mild symptomatic) is far reduced.  "It does not serve the purpose of better case management at individual level or a major dent in reducing transmission. Therefore, the revised policy by ICMR is epidemiologically sound. It will achieve public health purposes in an efficient way," Dr Lahariya said.Dr Chandrakant Lahariya also said that this new advisory, when combined with the new discharge policy, is a paradigm shift in public health response to the Covid-19 pandemic."  https://archive.ph/dUhbG

All  arrangements should be made to collect and transfer samples to testing facilities,  mapped to the health facility.  ? They are no longer required to pay fines for not covering their mouth. While the recent communication from the government said that flyers do not need to wear a mask, it still encouraged its usage. column79: "The debt moratorium will be available to individuals and small and medium enterprises that did not restructure their loans in 2020 and were classified as standard accounts till March 2021, Das said in an unscheduled virtual address. ... The moratoriums will be applicable to borrowers with a maximum total exposure of 250 million rupees ($3.39 million), Das said." - https://archive.ph/ZMwPq#selection-295.0-298.0 May 5 2021  https://web.archive.org/web/20230509142449/https://www.reuters.com/world/india/india-cenbank-allows-fresh-moratorium-some-small-borrowers-amid-covid-19-crisis-2021-05-05/  Some form of debt relief seems to be continuing, as seen from the national government recently approving further allocations to reimburse lenders to support the loan moratorium scheme, which would presumably in turn support the ability to offer debt relief for borrowers, including households. 1. 19 Jan 2022: "Goverment to pay Rs 974 crore more to lenders towards loan moratorium scheme" https://web.archive.org/web/20220120075321/https://www.newindianexpress.com/nation/2022/jan/19/govermentto-pay-rs-974-cr-more-to-lenders-towards-loan-moratorium-scheme-2408753.html 2. 20 Jan 2022: “By granting ex-gratia payment of difference between compound interest and simple interest during the six month moratorium period to distressed/vulnerable category of borrowers, irrespective of whether the borrower had availed of moratorium or not, the scheme would equitably help small borrowers bear the stress on account of the pandemic and get back on their feet, said an official release.” https://web.archive.org/web/20220207205127/https://zeenews.india.com/personal-finance/big-relief-for-borrowers-on-loan-moratorium-cabinet-sanctions-rs-973-crore-2429276.html 3. “The COVID-related restructuring scheme was first announced by Reserve Bank of India in August 2020 for both retail and corporate borrowers, and was then extended in May last year after a resurgence in COVID cases. The regulator had allowed banks to give a two-year moratorium in repayments under the restructuring scheme.”— https://web.archive.org/web/20220120185859/https://www.cnbctv18.com/finance/banks-seek-extension-of-covid-related-restructuring-amid-surge-in-coronavirus-cases-12185362.htm  There is a national scheme in place for debt relief. column90: https://archive.ph/jGI1E  ICMR Purposive testing strategy dated 10 Jan 2022  ""People who need not be tested: Contacts of confirmed cases of Covid unless identified as high risk based on age or comorbidities and individuals undertaking inter-state domestic travel," read the ICMR Advisory on Purposive Testing Strategy for COVID-19 issued on Monday.  The new strategy has invoked mixed reactions. Public health expert Dr Chandrakant Lahariya told India Today, "At this stage of the pandemic, especially when Omicron has a high rate of transmission and many are asymptomatic, the benefit of testing of asymptomatic (or even mild symptomatic) is far reduced.  "It does not serve the purpose of better case management at individual level or a major dent in reducing transmission. Therefore, the revised policy by ICMR is epidemiologically sound. It will achieve public health purposes in an efficient way," Dr Lahariya said.Dr Chandrakant Lahariya also said that this new advisory, when combined with the new discharge policy, is a paradigm shift in public health response to the Covid-19 pandemic."  https://archive.ph/dUhbG

column15: National overview as of 19 Jan: No nationwide school closure or student vaccine mandate has been imposed by the national govt (“Union govt”/”Centre”). However, several state governments have enacted school closures and other restrictions. While some areas (i.e Tamil Nadu) have enacted vaccine-differentiated restrictions, restrictions in many areas apply regardless of vaccination status.    Coding explanation: Unvaccinated and vaccinated are both coded 3G, to reflect the widespread closures found in at least *29* states/union territories, encompassing several of the most highly-populated regions. Note that vaccine-differentiated policies do exist, but states with such policies (I.e Tamil Nadu) have not yet opened schools for anyone, though it is planned to do so soon (1 Feb, for Tamil Nadu). Therefore, the coding is 3G to reflect how closure for vaccinated and unvaccinated is effectively the same for the time being, due to the same type of restriction (i.e physical closure of schools for everyone regardless of vaccination status). column24: Important note: Addition of vaccine-differentiated coding from this point.     1.	This indicator codes for physical closures/modified workplace requirements. (Example: Total closure of workplace, work-from-home requirements, orders to operate at 50% capacity instead).     2.	Additionally, vaccine-differentiation coding for this indicator records for requirements for visitors/customers to be vaccinated, *not staff/employees.* (Example: “Customers must show proof of vaccination to dine at a restaurant.”)    3.	For vaccine-differentiated measures for *staff/employees of workplaces*, please see indicator *V4* (Vaccine Mandates) instead. column74: For the period of 18—21 January, the protocol for international travellers emphasises differentiation mainly regarding whether the traveller is from an "At Risk" country or not, rather than vaccination status.     1. Screening:   - Regardless of vaccination status, all travellers must have a negative result on their PCR test no more than 72 hours before departure. Travellers must also complete and submit a declaration form on the Air Suvidha Portal.   - Upon arrival, travellers from "Countries Specified At Risk" must take a PCR test and may not leave the airport until they receive their result.  - Travellers who are not from such countries do not ordinarily need to be tested, but PCR tests are carried out on a random sample (2%) of this group.     2. Quarantine: All travellers, regardless of vaccination status and country of origin, must quarantine for 7 days. It is not possible to "test out" of quarantine, even if one tests negative on PCR test taken at the airport.     3. column15: Coding change: From 3G to 3T.    Coding explanation: As schools in several (but not all) states have fully or partly reopened on 1 Feb, the school closures have been downgraded from 3G (general) to 3T (targeted). However, please note that vaccine mandates for students do exist in some states that have reopened, but the strictest situation is coded for. The single "3T" coding is due to the *total closure* of schools in some areas as of 1 Feb, that *apply to both the vaccinated and unvaccinated*.     National overview: No nationwide restrictions imposed by national government, but many state-level closures and restrictions. Multiple states chose to reopen classes for at least some grades on 1 Feb, albeit with Covid-19 precautions (vaccine mandates for students, masking, sanitisation and social distancing rules). Meanwhile, total closures have continued in other areas—see list below. column42: As of March 1, the measures in place or planned in the following states or union territories are:    Andaman and Nicobar: An overnight 21:00-05:00 curfew is no longer active. Officials have lifted restrictions on tourist spots, other establishments, private vehicles, and gatherings. Public transport may operate at 75 percent capacity. Domestic travelers must hold negative results of a COVID-19 test taken within 48 hours before departure or vaccination certificates. Unvaccinated domestic travelers without pre-departure test results, as well as all entrants with an overseas travel history in the past 30 days, must take an on-arrival PCR test and quarantine until they receive a negative test result. Additional entry, testing, and quarantine rules are likely to enter tribal areas in the Nicobar Islands.    Andhra Pradesh: The 23:00-05:00 nightly curfew is no longer in place. Outdoor and indoor gatherings are capped at 200 and 100 people, respectively. Domestic arrivals must register online up to 72 hours before travel on the Andhra Pradesh police website. Domestic entrants do not require proof of vaccination or pre-departure testing; officials may direct symptomatic arrivals to undergo testing and/or quarantine based on test results.    Karnataka: Demonstrations are banned; permitted gatherings must be limited to 300 people if outdoors, and 200 people if indoors. Most in-person educational classes have resumed. Most venues, including state government offices, as well as dine-in, some recreational, and most sports facilities, may function at full capacity. Only fully vaccinated people can use dine-in, recreational, religious, and sports venues. Checkpoints and interstate transport curbs are most likely in border areas of Belagavi, Chamarajanagar, Dakshina Kannada, Kodagu, and Mysuru districts. Domestic arrivals must register online up to 72 hours before travel. Officials require entrants from Kerala, Goa, and Maharashtra states to provide a vaccine certificate.    Kerala: All arrivals must register online via the Jagratha portal up to 72 hours before travel. Unvaccinated entrants without pre-departure test results must take an on-arrival test and quarantine at home until they test negative or undergo a 14-day home quarantine. Pre-approved domestic travelers leaving the state within seven days are exempt from quarantine. On-arrival testing is limited to symptomatic and randomly selected international travelers. All international entrants are advised to self-monitor their health, submit to symptom surveillance, as well as avoid gatherings and crowded places for seven days from their arrival.    Puducherry: Large public gatherings remain prohibited through March 31, except permitted events such as funerals and weddings. Commercial, educational, and recreational venues, as well as transport services, can operate at full capacity. Retail outlets must ensure employees are vaccinated. Domestic entrants do not require proof of vaccination or pre-departure testing; officials may direct symptomatic arrivals to undergo testing and/or quarantine based on test results.    Tamil Nadu: All in-person educational classes have resumed statewide. Officials have lifted capacity limits on public transport as well as dine-in, grooming, sports, and retail venues. Staff at customer-facing positions and passengers on local suburban trains must be vaccinated. Public gatherings remain banned except for permitted events. Guest limits for weddings and funerals are 200 and 100, respectively. All domestic travelers must register online beforehand; those from Kerala must also carry proof of vaccination or negative pre-departure test results. Interstate travel curbs are possible, mainly to and from Kerala State.    https://web.archive.org/web/20220314103918/https://crisis24.garda.com/alerts/2022/02/india-kerala-state-lifts-most-covid-19-curbs-as-of-march-1-update-47
